Arnold Split Workout

The Arnold split combines chest with back on the same day and shoulders with arms on the same day — pairing opposing muscle groups for efficient training and potential superset work. This structure is repeated twice per week across 6 training days.

Advanced 📅 6 days/week ⏱ 75–90 min
📚 Professor Splits' Guide

The Arnold split packs a lot of work into each week. Treat the second pass of each muscle as the lighter one, and take a lighter week every few weeks so fatigue does not build up.

Overview

This is the split Arnold Schwarzenegger reportedly used during his Mr. Olympia winning years. It pairs agonist and antagonist muscle groups — chest and back together, shoulders and arms together — which creates an unusual pump and allows for superset work that saves training time while maintaining high volume.

The Arnold split is for advanced trainees with years of consistent training who want a high-volume, high-frequency approach. It demands 6 days per week and 75–90 minute sessions — not for the faint-hearted or the beginner.

✅ Pros
  • High frequency — each muscle trained twice per week like PPL.
  • Interesting pairing — chest/back supersets are uniquely effective.
  • High volume accumulation over 6 days.
  • Classic, proven structure with legendary results to its name.
⚠️ Cons
  • Very high time commitment — 6 days, 75–90 minutes each.
  • Recovery demands are extreme — not suitable for drug-free beginners.
  • Chest and back together is a very long session.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did Arnold actually use this split?▾
Arnold has described training with high frequency and volume during his competitive years, with sessions pairing chest/back and shoulders/arms. Whether this exact template matches his historical training precisely is debatable, but the structure captures his documented training philosophy.
Is the Arnold split too much volume?▾
For most natural trainees, yes — this is an extreme amount of volume and frequency. Consider whether you have years of training under your belt and excellent recovery habits (sleep, nutrition, low stress) before attempting this programme.
